window: short-window protocol: hard recovery unit (+2400 s) armed before any stop; qwen-inference-health.timer suspended for the window and restored; maintenance lease held; baseline restored and authenticated
warmup: one unprofiled 128-token completion before profiling absorbed the ~263 s serving-start Triton JIT storm (largest single compile: _fused_rotate_balance_quantize 20.03 s)

profiler.method: POST /start_profile {output_dir=/cache/prof, activities=[GPU], num_steps=2} — auto-stop bounded the capture to the prefill; /stop_profile correctly returned 500 (already stopped)

microbatch_structure_measured.expected_from_source: 2 chunks x 16 full-attention layers x 128 eight-query micro-iterations (kvarn_backend.forward_extend loops range(0,1024,8)) = 4096
microbatch_structure_measured.note: the 8-query loop is launch-count heavy but time-light: 37594 store launches total only 134.8 ms (mean 3.6 us)

depth_attribution.split_mean_growth_chunk1_to_chunk2: 4.6x for a 2x cached-prefix growth, superlinear because mean visible prefix per query rises faster than page count alone
depth_attribution.depth_invariant_buckets: marlin count per chunk constant (524 total, ~262/chunk), gdn flat, store flat: only _packed_attention_split carries the depth-linear slope
depth_attribution.conclusion: the quadratic prefill term is ~entirely _packed_attention_split; its share of GPU busy rises from 47% (chunk 1) to 71% (chunk 2) and keeps rising with depth

kernel_efficiency_estimate.split_throughput_chunk2: ~0.26 TFLOP/s fp32-equivalent for the attention arithmetic it performs
kernel_efficiency_estimate.sm86_reference: ~35 TFLOP/s fp32 SIMT, ~140 TFLOP/s bf16 tensor-core dense
structural_causes_from_source: one program per (8-query microbatch is further split per single query, per head): scores computed as fp32 multiply-reduce, no tensor-core matmul
each of the 24 query-head programs re-reads its kv-head's packed page data: 6x redundant KV traffic per GQA group
per-token committed/provisional mask bytes re-read per query-head program
byte-wise 4-bit/2-bit dequant arithmetic recomputed per query-head
BLOCK=32 token tiles inside a 128-token page loop; split-KV SPLITS axis multiplies metadata work at depth

implications: Repair of the 40-70x depth gap is a single-kernel problem: rewrite _packed_attention_split for chunk prefill with query tiling over tensor cores, one dequantized KV load shared across the 6-head GQA group, and mask reads amortized per page block; the achieved 0.7%-of-fp32-peak leaves two orders of magnitude of headroom against the ~26x needed to fit 262144 tokens in the 1800 s cap.

The 8-query microbatch loop and the 37594-launch store pipeline are a launch-tax and code-clarity problem, not the time bottleneck (2.6% of busy); batching them is worthwhile in the same patch stage but will not alone close the gap.
GDN sequential extend is exonerated by measurement: 0.68% of GPU busy with flat per-chunk cost.
The Marlin W4A16 GEMMs (27.6%) bound any repair: even a perfect attention kernel leaves ~1.1-1.4 s/chunk floor at this depth, consistent with the dense FP8 reference behavior.
limitations: GPU-only capture: no CPU-side op/launch-gap timeline; the 8% non-busy span is inferred, not attributed.
Two chunks, depth <=2048: the slope attribution at larger depths relies on the two-window fit cross-check, not in-trace measurement.
Profiler overhead on this launch-heavy path is unquantified; segment walls may be inflated a few percent relative to the unprofiled window-1 chunk lines at matching depth.
One request; not capacity, numerics or quality evidence.
